blocks.content: This concluding chapter consolidates key personalities and every important numeric/name/date fact from the preceding chapters into one place for rapid last-minute revision before the exam.

cells: Founder-leader of the Mizo National Front (MNF); led the 1966-1986 insurgency; signed the 1986 Peace Accord; became interim CM of the UT (Chapter 3)
First Chief Minister of Mizoram (of the Union Territory), from 3 May 1972 (Chapter 4)
Prime Minister of India who signed the Mizoram Peace Accord with Laldenga, 30 June 1986 (Chapter 3)
Long-serving former Chief Minister of Mizoram (MNF), preceded Lalduhoma; a senior MNF leader with deep roots in the insurgency-era movement
Current (2026) Chief Minister of Mizoram (ZPM), since 8 December 2023; former IPS officer; first MP in India disqualified under the anti-defection law (Chapter 5)
Current (2026) Governor of Mizoram; former Chief of the Army Staff and Union Minister (Chapter 5)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Track the Chief Ministerial arc: Laldenga (interim, 1986 post-Accord) -> C. Chhunga (first elected CM of the UT era, 1972, predating Laldenga's later tenure) -> decades of Congress-MNF alternation (including Zoramthanga) -> Lalduhoma/ZPM (since 2023) — a useful organising political-history thread for Mizoram.

items: Mizoram: approx 21,081 sq km; borders Assam, Manipur, Tripura, Myanmar, Bangladesh; capital: Aizawl.
Terrain: steep, parallel, north-south hill ranges; virtually no flat land; highest point: Phawngpui ('Blue Mountain', ~2,157 m).
'Mautam' (~48-year bamboo mass-flowering) causes rat-population explosions and famine; the 1959 famine triggered the MNF's formation.
Mizo oral tradition: origin at 'Chhinlung'; close ties to Chin (Myanmar) and Kuki-Zo (Manipur) communities.
Lushai Hills annexed by the British in 1890; administered as an 'Excluded Area'.
MNF (1961, Laldenga) launched armed insurgency 1 March 1966; IAF bombed Aizawl 5 March 1966; Peace Accord signed 30 June 1986.
UT status from 21 January 1972; full statehood (23rd state) on 20 February 1987 — same date as Arunachal Pradesh.
Article 371G (53rd Amendment, 1986): protects Mizo land, customary law, religious/social practices from Parliament without Assembly consent — similar to Nagaland's Article 371A.
3 Sixth Schedule ADCs for minorities within Mizoram: Chakma, Mara, Lai.
40-seat Assembly. Current CM: Lalduhoma (ZPM, since 8 Dec 2023); Governor: Gen. V.K. Singh (Retd.).
Gauhati High Court has a permanent Bench at Aizawl (no separate Mizoram High Court).
Jhum cultivation historically dominant; New Land Use Policy (NLUP) promotes settled horticulture; Bana Kaih Scheme is the current flagship initiative.
Population (2011) approx 10.97 lakh; ST share approx 94-95%; Christian share approx 87%; literacy approx 91-92% (2nd highest after Kerala in several rankings).
Mizo (Duhlian) = official language, Kuki-Chin-Mizo (Zo) branch of Tibeto-Burman.
Cheraw ('Bamboo Dance') is the iconic traditional dance; Chapchar Kut (spring) is the flagship festival.
Phawngpui National Park, Murlen National Park, and Dampa Tiger Reserve are key protected areas.
Revise this chapter last — it consolidates every numeric/name/date fact from Chapters 1-10 in one place for rapid recall.
The single most important sequence to never confuse: 1959 Mautam famine -> 1961 MNF formed -> 1966 insurgency begins -> 1986 Peace Accord -> 1987 statehood.
Always verify current officeholders (Governor, CM) closer to your exam date.
